findings.claim: getAllowedLocations is gated only by GET_LOCATIONS (a privilege core grants to the Authenticated role, so every logged-in user holds it) yet it resolves the target user through dao.getUser(user.getUserId()) at line 860, an unadvised @Repository call, so the GET_USERS privilege that gates every other User read on UserService never fires and any authenticated user can read any other user's stored location assignment by iterating userIds.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, any authenticated user can enumerate every other user's assigned locations (in the deployments this feature targets, that is the staff-by-department/ward roster), because AuthorizationAdvice only checks the declared GET_LOCATIONS - already held by the Authenticated role - and the User row is then fetched through HibernateUserDAO, which AOPConfig.createAdvisor does not intercept, so the GET_USERS gate on UserService.getUser is bypassed. Nothing throws and nothing is logged, so the disclosure is invisible; and once the companion REST PR (webservices.rest#762) and esm-login-app depend on this signature, tightening the privilege becomes a breaking API change rather than a one-line edit.
findings.evidence: RAN, in the prepared worktree at b7cd909d245086fa10691496f88e5ec6971b77c2: a throwaway probe test (api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/api/SecLensProbeTest.java, since deleted; `JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk-21.jdk/Contents/Home mvn -o -pl api test -Dtest=SecLensProbeTest -Dspotless.check.skip=true -Dspotless.apply.skip=true` -> Tests run: 5, Failures: 0, Errors: 0). It assigned user 1 to location 2, created a fresh non-superuser 'probecaller' with no privilege-bearing role, authenticated as them, and printed: `PROBE3 authenticated=probecaller isSuperUser=false hasGetUsers=false hasGetLocations=true`. POSITIVE CONTROL in that same context: `userService.getUser(1)` -> `PROBE3 control threw APIAuthenticationException` (so the GET_USERS gate really is unsatisfied for this caller). Then `userService.getAllowedLocations(u, tag)` where `u = new User(); u.setUserId(1);` -> `PROBE3 leaked=[Xanadu]`, i.e. it returned user 1's persisted user_location assignment. READ: UserServiceImpl.java:856 `@Authorized(PrivilegeConstants.GET_LOCATIONS)` and :860 `dao.getUser(user.getUserId())`; UserService.java:86 `@Authorized({ PrivilegeConstants.GET_USERS }) User getUser(Integer userId)`; HibernateUserDAO.java:59 `@Repository("userDAO")`; AOPConfig.java `createAdvisor` matches `targetClass.isAnnotationPresent(Service.class)` only, and UserServiceImpl.java:70 is `@Service("userService")` while the DAO is not - so DAO calls carry no authorization advice. Blast radius established from core's own shipped data: the single role_privilege row for 'Get Locations' in api/src/main/resources/org/openmrs/liquibase/snapshots/core-data/liquibase-core-data-2.9.x.xml grants it to role 'Authenticated' (extracted by parsing every <insert tableName="role_privilege"> block). Sibling check: every other UserService method that resolves a User from the datastore requires GET_USERS; the two that are only @Authorized() (getLastLoginTime, getDefaultLocaleForUser) read fields off the object the caller already holds (HibernateUserDAO.java:806 `user.getUserProperty(...)`, UserServiceImpl.java:797) rather than re-reading the row, so they are not a precedent for this. Fix, mirroring the in-tree guard at UserServiceImpl.java:431 (setUserProperty): allow the call for the authenticated user's own record and require GET_USERS otherwise. If you prefer the annotation, it must be `@Authorized(value = {PrivilegeConstants.GET_USERS, PrivilegeConstants.GET_LOCATIONS}, requireAll = true)` - Authorized.requireAll() defaults to false, so simply adding GET_USERS to the array would weaken the check, not strengthen it.

findings.claim: The new native `delete from user_location where location_id = :locationId` silently converts every user whose assignment set it empties from restricted to unrestricted, because an empty set means 'all tagged locations'; the row count returned by executeUpdate() is discarded, user_location carries no audit columns, and nothing is logged, so the widening leaves no trace at all.
findings.evidence: RAN (same probe run as security-1): `probe2_purgeLastAssignedLocation` tagged locations 1 and 2 as 'Login Location', created and tagged a third location, assigned user 1 to that location alone, and printed `PROBE2 before=[Probe Ward]`. It then called `locationService.purgeLocation(...)` on that one location and re-read, printing `PROBE2 after=[Unknown Location, Xanadu]` - the user went from one allowed location to every tagged location in the system. READ: HibernateLocationDAO.java:133-134 discards the `executeUpdate()` count; UserServiceImpl.java:868-869 `if (assigned == null || assigned.isEmpty()) return tagged;` is the fail-open branch; the liquibase changeset (liquibase-update-to-latest-3.0.x.xml:152-160) creates user_location with no audit columns; `git grep -n user_location -- api/src/main omod/src` shows nothing logs or records the deletion. Note retireLocation (LocationServiceImpl.java:257) does not touch user_location, so only purge triggers this. Not blocking: fail-open on an empty set is the ticket's explicit design ('The caller always receives a usable list'), purgeLocation requires PURGE_LOCATIONS, and the alternative (deny) would lock the user out. Concrete fix: keep the count from executeUpdate() and log at WARN when it is non-zero, naming the location, so an admin purge that un-restricts users is at least traceable; and state the consequence where an implementer will read it - the User.locations javadoc (User.java:101-107) says an empty set means unrestricted but not that any path which empties the set therefore grants access to every tagged location.

findings.claim: Nothing enforces the restriction anywhere - getAllowedLocations is an advisory filter for a picker, not an access control - but the PR title ('restricting users to assigned locations') and the javadoc ('the locations the given user is allowed to use') both read as enforcement, which invites a deployment to treat user_location as a security boundary it is not.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED by positive search rather than a zero-hit: `git grep -n "getAllowedLocations"` over the whole tree returns only the declaration (UserService.java:669), the impl (UserServiceImpl.java:857), the User javadoc reference (User.java:104) and the new tests - no in-core consumer. `git grep -n "getLocations()" -- api/src/main/java` returns 8 hits (so the pipeline finds real matches), of which the only reader of User.locations is UserServiceImpl.java:867; the Obs/Visit hits are unrelated search-criteria getters. LocationService.getLocationsByTag (the call the current esm-login-app makes via /ws/rest/v1/location?tag=Login+Location) is unchanged and still returns every tagged location to every GET_LOCATIONS holder, and no encounter/visit/login path consults User.locations. So a restricted user can still obtain and submit any location. The ticket (TRUNK-6669, read at the REST API) frames the problem as a 'noisy picker', which supports the advisory reading - hence a question rather than a finding: is advisory-only the intent, and if so is it worth saying in the javadoc that this scopes a picker and is not an authorization check? Related and worth an answer in the same breath: the PR adds no privilege of its own for managing assignments, so writing User.locations rides EDIT_USERS via saveUser with no self-assignment guard, whereas role assignment on the same method is additionally constrained by checkPrivileges (UserServiceImpl.java:407-416). That asymmetry is defensible exactly as long as locations are not enforced.

what_i_swept: Verified the diff stat first (git diff 28e3bab9e206170df7fd43cf709495b6d45fe16a b7cd909d245086fa10691496f88e5ec6971b77c2 = 8 files, +216/-6, matches). Read the PR body and TRUNK-6669 with its comments via the unauthenticated JIRA REST endpoint. Then swept my dimension as follows. AUTHORIZATION: enumerated every @Authorized on UserService by parsing the file, compared the new method against all of them, and traced the privilege gate end to end - AOPConfig.createAdvisor (advises only @Service targets), AuthorizationAdvice.before, Authorized.requireAll() semantics, UserContext.hasPrivilege(String, boolean) including proxy handling - then established the blast radius from core's shipped role_privilege data rather than assuming. Confirmed empirically with a runtime probe carrying a positive control (security-1). INPUT VALIDATION: exercised every argument branch of getAllowedLocations - null user, null tag, transient user (no userId), userId that does not resolve - all fail closed to an empty list; noted the method ignores every caller-supplied field except userId (a defensive choice that is also what makes the missing GET_USERS check exploitable with a bare `new User()`). INJECTION: both native queries are constant SQL with a compile-time String constant spliced only into the parameter *name* and the value bound via setParameter; the CTE's only concatenated fragment (retiredFilter) is a fixed literal chosen by a boolean. No user-controlled string reaches SQL. SECRETS / CI: grepped the diff for password/secret/api-key/token/credential/PEM markers with a positive control (a `user_location` grep on the same file returned 11 hits first); the only hit is a pre-existing test credential in unchanged context. No CI, workflow, or Dockerfile touched. UNSAFE DESERIALIZATION: User is Serializable and now carries the new collection; confirmed Location implements java.io.Serializable (Location.java:54) so HTTP-session serialization is intact, and no untrusted deserialization path is introduced. OUTWARD TRACE, one level past the diff and beyond: (1) WRITE PATHS for the new authorization-relevant field - audited every path in UserServiceImpl that persists a User, and found that saveUserProperty/saveUserProperties are only @Authorized() (merely authenticated) and merge Context.getAuthenticatedUser() via dao.saveUser, bypassing saveUser's requirePrivilege(EDIT_USERS) and checkPrivileges. I probed this as a self-service escalation vector and it is NOT one: the lazy collection on the detached authenticated User stays uninitialised, Hibernate's merge skips uninitialised collections, and the rows survive unchanged (PROBE1 before=1/after=1, PROBE1b before=1/after=1 across a re-authentication); forcing initialisation is not even possible, since Context.getAuthenticatedUser().getLocations() throws LazyInitializationException (no session). Cleared, no finding. (2) LIFECYCLE - checked the other side of both new foreign keys: Hibernate owns the join table from the User side (@JoinTable is on User), so purgeUser cleans up, which is why only the Location side needed the manual delete; retireLocation does not touch the table at all. (3) ENVERS - User is @Audited and the new collection is not @NotAudited, same shape as the audited `roles` collection, and envers ships disabled (hibernate.integration.envers.enabled=false) with no _AUD/_audit tables in liquibase, so this is not a divergence. (4) AUDIT COLUMNS - the new table has none, but neither does user_role, core's actual RBAC mapping table, so the project's own precedent settles it and I dropped that candidate. (5) CONSUMERS - established by positive search that no in-core code enforces the new field, and that the pre-existing getLocationsByTag path the frontend uses is unchanged (security-3). Two passes: pass 1 produced security-1/2/3; pass 2 (write paths, envers, audit columns, serialization, secrets, injection, FK lifecycle, retire path) confirmed those and surfaced nothing substantive in my dimension, which satisfies the convergence rule.
out_of_scope: CORRECTNESS: the new comment at HibernateLocationDAO.java:129-132 asserts 'Safe today since no caller holds a loaded User across this call' - falsified. `userService.getUser(1); u.getLocations().size(); locationService.purgeLocation(loc);` in one session throws org.hibernate.TransientPropertyValueException: "Persistent instance of 'org.openmrs.User' references an unsaved transient instance of 'org.openmrs.Location' ... [org.openmrs.User.locations -> org.openmrs.Location]" (my probe2b, ran green as a captured exception). The PR's own new LocationServiceTest#purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationAssignedToAUser misses it because it never reads the collection back before purging; the fix the comment itself names (evict/refresh, or flush+clear before session.remove) is what is needed.

API DESIGN: Context.getAuthenticatedUser().getLocations() throws LazyInitializationException ('Cannot lazily initialize collection of role org.openmrs.User.locations with key 1 (no session)') because the authenticated User is detached - so the new public getter is unusable on the User instance the platform passes around most, and neither the getter (User.java:372) nor the field javadoc warns about it.

CORRECTNESS: getAllowedLocations returns the live list from getLocationsByTag directly in the unrestricted branch but a fresh collected list in the restricted branch, so callers get differently-owned lists from the same method.
ROBUSTNESS: saveUser accepts a Set<Location> containing a null element without complaint and silently persists nothing for it (observed incidentally when a probe passed a non-existent location id).

STYLE: splicing LOCATION_ID into the SQL string to form ':' + "locationId" (HibernateLocationDAO.java:133) reads like SQL string-building at a glance even though it is safe; keeping ':locationId' literal in the query and using the constant only in setParameter would be plainer.
could_not_verify: In the security-1 probe, GET_LOCATIONS was supplied to the test caller via Context.addProxyPrivilege rather than through a persisted role: building the role in-test left hasGetLocations=false (the role-privilege cache did not pick up a privilege and role created in the same test transaction). AuthorizationAdvice resolves the gate through Context.hasPrivilege, which treats proxy and role privileges identically, and the load-bearing half of the experiment - that GET_USERS was genuinely absent from the caller's role graph - was proved directly by the positive control (getUser(1) threw APIAuthenticationException). So the bypass is established, but the GET_LOCATIONS half came from a proxy privilege, not a role.

The companion REST change (openmrs-module-webservices.rest#762) is in another repository and was not reviewed; its /user/{uuid}/location resource resolves the uuid through a GET_USERS-gated lookup, so the disclosure in security-1 is reachable from in-JVM callers (modules, admin scripting) rather than from that particular REST path. Whether any other REST or module caller passes a caller-supplied userId straight into getAllowedLocations is unverified.

notes: Reviewed at b7cd909d245086fa10691496f88e5ec6971b77c2 against merge base 28e3bab9e206170df7fd43cf709495b6d45fe16a; stat matched the stated 8 files / +216 / -6. Per instructions I did not read the PR's review conversation, so anything below may already have been raised there - the PR body shows several prior review rounds. The three findings are ordered by how much they matter and are independent, except that security-3's answer changes how seriously security-2 should be taken: if the restriction is only ever a picker filter then silent widening on purge is cosmetic, and if any deployment is expected to lean on it as a boundary then both security-2 and the missing self-assignment guard get heavier. Worth recording what came out clean, since these were the scariest hypotheses and a later reviewer would otherwise re-run them: the self-service write path (saveUserProperty, merely authenticated, bypasses EDIT_USERS and checkPrivileges) cannot alter or wipe user_location rows; there is no SQL injection in either native query; no secrets and no CI config in the diff; purgeUser is covered because Hibernate owns the join table from the User side; and the missing audit columns match user_role, core's own RBAC mapping table. One process note: the evidence for security-1 and security-2 came from a single throwaway test class (api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/api/SecLensProbeTest.java) which I deleted afterwards; `git status --porcelain` in the worktree is empty and no tracked file was mutated at any point.
